title: The Worst Sunday Night Game Ever Made, and I'll Be Watching Every Second
seoTitle: Commanders vs. Eagles Prediction: Sunday Night, Alex Moore's Flags and Life After Terry
summary: Commanders vs. Eagles on Sunday night: the most flag-happy ref in the NFL, a week without Terry, a cornerback's guarantee, and my number.
wireTaps: Who steps up with Terry out? Make your case.
paragraphs: The Athletic ran a piece this week ranking the worst Sunday Night Football games since 2006, and they wrote it because of us. The Eagles are 2-5. We're 1-4-1. Add it up and NBC has handed the whole country a matchup with a combined record of 3-9-1, in prime time, on Halloween weekend. I have never been more excited for anything in my life.

Two links before we start, because I keep hiding the good stuff at the bottom: [who's reffing Sunday](whos-reffing.html) (it matters this week, trust me), and [Call Your Shot](leaderboard.html), where you can beat me at picking scores. It's not hard.

Here's my problem with this division. If any NFC East team had just taken off this year, I could have mentally checked out by Halloween and gotten into woodworking or something. But nope. The Giants are in first at 4-2-1. Dallas is 3-4. The Eagles have lost five in a row. Washington has done exactly, precisely, just enough to keep us interested. Chris summed it up in the group chat with a GIF from a bar show: "There are no losers at Barmageddon. We are all losers." He captioned it "king of the losers." Sunday night, one of us gets the crown.
## Ref Watch: Bring Snacks

Every Tuesday, Football Zebras posts who's refereeing every game, and this week we drew Alex Moore. I looked him up. His crews throw more flags than any referee in the NFL: 17 a game, against a league average of 13.3, the most of the 17 refs with enough games to rank. That's almost four extra flags a game, which is roughly eleven extra minutes of me standing up from the couch to yell at a man in a striped shirt who cannot hear me.

Here's the good news, and I mean that, which is rare for this section of a Commanders post. Road teams draw 9.2 flags a game from his crews. Home teams draw 7.8. We're home. For once, the math is wearing burgundy. Last time he had us was 2025, against the Bears: five flags on us, nine on them, and I'd like that exact ratio again, please.

The whole breakdown is on the [Ref Watch page](whos-reffing.html): every game Moore has worked these two seasons, our flags game by game, and every referee ranked. It updates every week, so bookmark it and come back each Tuesday to find out who to blame on Sunday.
## Terry

Terry McLaurin tore his patellar tendon against the 49ers, and this week he went on injured reserve. He's done for the year. Monday, the group chat was arguing over a list of the most underrated Washington players of the last 25 years, and I put Terry on it: a third-round pick who kept posting 1,000-yard seasons while catching passes from a revolving door of quarterbacks. I wrote that on Monday. It hit different by Wednesday.
Get well, Terry. Take all the time you need. We'll be here, mostly because we don't know how to leave.

So now it's Antonio Williams' turn. Back in the preseason, I said the rookie had some McLaurin to his game, and I said it with every possible caveat. Sunday night we find out how much. The team also promoted Van Jefferson to the active roster, Treylon Burks is questionable with a foot, and Stefon Diggs sat out Wednesday's practice, which is the kind of thing I've learned to read about with one eye closed.
## Everybody's Guaranteeing Things

Amik Robertson guaranteed a win this week. A guarantee. From a 1-4-1 team. I respect it enormously, the way you respect a guy who walks into a casino with his rent money and a really good feeling. Stefon Diggs added that Dan Quinn has done a great, let's say, "very" job, and that the team just has to "see one go through the hoop." I don't know what sport that is, but I'm in. And Steve Wilks, who the team brought in to help with game plans after San Francisco, will now be on the sideline for games too, starting Sunday. That's three new things for a defense that just needed one.
Vegas has us favored by six. I have never been less comfortable being favored in my life. Being the favorite is a Commanders fan's natural predator.

Some perspective, courtesy of Chris: our last win was September 27, against Seattle. He pointed out that if you'd started a family that night, the baby would be crawling by now. I don't think that's how babies work. I also didn't argue, because it feels true.
## The Group Chat Goes to History Class

That underrated-players argument turned into a full all-time team, and it went about how you'd expect. Chris looked at the offense and said, "TBH, the offense list makes me sad. Basically no one good from our fandom." Then he asked who Jerry Smith was. Jerry Smith was a great tight end for us in the '60s and '70s, Chris, and you graduated in '01, so I'll allow it. Jason said his true fandom started in 2000: "I liked them in the '90s, but I didn't know anything, and they blew." Which means all three of us signed up for this team at the exact moment it stopped being good, and none of us have left. That's not loyalty. That's a hostage situation with tailgating.
## My Number

I'm 0-2 on the leaderboard. My Giants pick lost to a tie and my birthday pick lost to the 49ers, which means I'm currently being outpicked by Taylor P, who has picked exactly one game. This week: Commanders 27, Eagles 13. That's bold. So bold. But we're due.
Your turn. [Call your shot](leaderboard.html), put a name on it, and get on the board. The season winner gets a sticker and a year of bragging rights over me, which, so far, is not a high bar.

I'll be home for this one, on my couch, where God intended. These 8:20 kickoffs are killing me, and that's on a weekend when UVA football isn't even keeping me out late on Saturday. I'm 45 now. My body has formally objected to anything that ends after midnight, and Sunday night football ends after midnight on purpose. I'll be there anyway. The flags alone could push this thing past 12:30.

Here's the hope part, because there's always a hope part. The Eagles have lost five straight. The division leader is 4-2-1. Our quarterback is healthy, our rookie gets his shot, and the most flag-happy ref in football hates road teams more than home teams. It's the worst Sunday night game ever made, and it's ours. Hail.
